text.p: Coca-Cola Co. said Tuesday it has formed Coca-Cola Nordic Beverages, a joint venture with Carlsberg A/S of Denmark as its Nordic "anchor" bottler.
In Coca-Cola's worldwide bottling system, anchor bottlers are those in which the Atlanta-based company holds a large stake.
Carlsberg holds a 51 percent stake in the venture and Coca-Cola holds 49 percent, the company said.
Coca-Cola Nordic, to be based in Copenhagen, will act as a holding company for operations in Denmark and Sweden and later in Norway, and have rights to bottle and distribute Coca-Cola products.
The venture is subject to regulatory approval by the European Union. The approval process could take a few months, according to a Coca-Cola spokesman.

"The creation of a Nordic anchor bottler creates a dynamic new business system in the region and establishes a framework for future growth and for serving our customers and consumers in the best possible way," said M. Douglas Ivester, president and chief operating officer of Coca-Cola.
Coca-Cola's stock edged up 12.5 cents to $59.875 on the New York Stock Exchange in late morning trading.
